ei.title: Shift in the Work-Time Paradigm Brought About by Industrialization

fullPassage: The arrival of the Industrial Age changed the relationship among time, labor, and capital. Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with greater speed and volume than ever before. A machine that runs twelve hours a day will produce more widgets than one that runs for only eight hours per day ― and a machine that runs twenty-four hours per day will produce the most widgets of all. As such, at many factories, the workday is divided into eight-hour shifts, so that there will always be people on hand to keep the widget machines humming. Industrialization raised the potential value of every single work hour ― the more hours you worked, the more widgets you produced, and the more money you made ― and thus wages became tied to effort and production. Labor, previously guided by harvest cycles, became clock-oriented, and society started to reorganize around new principles of productivity.

questions.passage: The arrival of the Industrial Age changed the relationship among time, labor, and capital. Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with greater speed and volume than ever before. A machine ①<u>that</u> runs twelve hours a day will produce more widgets than one that runs for only eight hours per day ― and a machine that runs twenty-four hours per day will produce the most widgets of all. As such, at many factories, the workday is ②<u>dividing</u> into eight-hour shifts, so that there will always be people on hand to keep the widget machines humming. Industrialization raised the potential value of every single work hour ― the more hours you worked, the more widgets you ③<u>produced</u>, and the more money you made ― and thus wages became tied to effort and production. Labor, previously guided by harvest cycles, became clock-oriented, and society started to ④<u>reorganize</u> around new principles of productivity.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① that: 선행사 A machine 뒤 관계대명사 — 적절.
✅ ② dividing: 근무일이 '나뉘는' 수동의 의미이므로 is divided가 맞음. is dividing(능동 진행형)은 부적절.
❌ ③ produced: the more ~, the more ~ 구문 내 과거시제 — 적절.
❌ ④ reorganize: started to + 동사원형 — 적절.
det.tip: 수동태 be + p.p.: is divided(나뉘다). 주어(workday)가 '나누어지는' 대상이므로 수동태.

questions.passage: The arrival of the Industrial Age ①<u>changed</u> the relationship among time, labor, and capital. Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with ②<u>greater</u> speed and volume than ever before. A machine that runs twelve hours a day will produce more widgets than one that runs for only eight hours per day ― and a machine that runs twenty-four hours per day will produce the most widgets of all. As such, at many factories, the workday is divided into eight-hour shifts, so that there will always be people on hand to keep the widget machines humming. Industrialization raised the potential value of every single work hour ― the more hours you worked, the more widgets you produced, and the more money you made ― and thus wages became tied to effort and production. Labor, previously guided by harvest cycles, became clock-oriented, and society started ③<u>reorganize</u> around new principles of ④<u>productivity</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① changed: 과거시제 동사 — 적절.
❌ ② greater: 비교급 형용사, than과 호응 — 적절.
✅ ③ reorganize: start는 to부정사나 동명사를 목적어로 취함. 동사원형 단독 불가. started to reorganize가 맞음.
❌ ④ productivity: 전치사 of의 목적어로 명사 — 적절.
det.tip: start + to V / Ving: started to reorganize 또는 started reorganizing.

questions.passage: The arrival of the Industrial Age changed the relationship among time, labor, and capital. Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with greater speed and volume than ever before. A machine ①<u>what</u> runs twelve hours a day will produce more widgets than one that runs for only eight hours per day ― and a machine that runs twenty-four hours per day will produce the most widgets of all. As such, at many factories, the workday is divided into eight-hour shifts, so that there will always be people ②<u>on hand</u> to keep the widget machines humming. Industrialization raised the potential value of every single work hour ― ③<u>the more</u> hours you worked, the more widgets you produced, and the more money you made ― and thus wages became ④<u>tied</u> to effort and production.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① what: 선행사 A machine이 있으므로 관계대명사 that이 맞음. what은 선행사를 포함하므로 불가.
❌ ② on hand: '가까이에' 숙어 — 적절.
❌ ③ the more: 'the 비교급 ~, the 비교급 ~' 구문 — 적절.
❌ ④ tied: became tied to(~에 연결되다) 과거분사 보어 — 적절.
det.tip: 관계대명사 what(선행사 포함) vs that(선행사 필요). A machine that runs(돌아가는 기계).

questions.passage: The arrival of the Industrial Age changed the relationship among time, labor, and capital. Industrialization ①<u>raised</u> the potential value of every single work hour ― the more hours you worked, the more widgets you ②<u>produced</u>, and the more money you made ― and thus wages became tied to effort and production. Labor, previously guided by harvest cycles, became ③<u>nature-oriented</u>, and society started to ④<u>reorganize</u> around new principles of productivity.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① raised: 산업화가 가치를 '끌어올렸다' — 원문 그대로.
❌ ② produced: 위젯을 '생산했다' — 원문 그대로.
✅ ③ nature-oriented: 원문은 clock-oriented(시계 중심의). 산업화 이후 노동이 '자연 중심'이 되었다는 건 시계 중심으로 전환된 맥락과 정반대.
❌ ④ reorganize: 사회가 '재편'하기 시작했다 — 원문 그대로.
det.tip: clock-oriented(시계 중심) = 산업화 이후. nature-oriented(자연 중심) = 산업화 이전(harvest cycles).

Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with greater speed and volume than ever before. As such, at many factories, the workday is ③<u>divided</u> into eight-hour shifts, so that there will always be people on hand to keep the widget machines humming. questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① changed: 산업화가 관계를 '바꾸었다' — 원문 그대로.
✅ ② fewer: 원문은 more(더 많은). 12시간 기계가 8시간 기계보다 '더 적은' 위젯을 생산한다는 건 이후 '24시간 기계가 가장 많이 생산'한다는 논리와 모순.
❌ ③ divided: 근무일이 '나뉜다' — 원문 그대로.
❌ ④ tied: 임금이 노력에 '연결되었다' — 원문 그대로.
det.tip: 12시간 > 8시간 = 더 많이(more) 생산. fewer는 정반대.

Labor, previously guided by harvest cycles, became clock-oriented, and society started to reorganize around ④<u>old</u> principles of productivity.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① greater: '더 큰' 속도와 규모 — 원문 그대로.
❌ ② made: '더 많은 돈을 벌었다' — 원문 그대로.
❌ ③ effort: 임금이 '노력'과 생산에 연결 — 원문 그대로.
✅ ④ old: 원문은 new(새로운). 사회가 '오래된' 생산성 원리로 재편된다는 건 산업화 이후 '새로운' 패러다임이라는 흐름과 정반대.
det.tip: 산업화 = 새로운(new) 원리로 전환. old는 이전 수확 주기 시대.

Labor, previously guided by harvest cycles, became clock-oriented, and society started to reorganize around new principles of productivity. The passage mainly argues that industrialization __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 산업화가 시간을 노동의 가치 단위로 바꾸었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ turned time into the fundamental measure of labor and wages: 시간당 생산·임금 연결이 본문 핵심.
❌ ① eliminated the need for human workers at factories: 본문은 오히려 교대 인력 배치.
❌ ② preserved traditional harvest-based labor practices: 수확 기반은 대체된 이전 방식.
❌ ④ shortened the average workday for factory employees: 본문은 교대로 24시간 가동.
det.tip: 핵심: time → labor's value measure. 시간 = 임금 = 생산성.

ch: eliminated the need for human workers at factories
turned time into the fundamental measure of labor and wages
shortened the average workday for factory employees

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 사회 전체가 기계가 정한 시간 리듬에 맞춰 재편되었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① the rhythm of machines replaced the rhythm of nature in organizing society: 수확 주기(자연)에서 시계(기계 리듬)로의 전환이 본문 전체 논지.
❌ ② farmers became wealthier than factory workers after industrialization: 농부·공장 노동자 부의 비교는 본문 없음.
❌ ③ machines eventually stopped running because workers refused shifts: 기계 중단은 본문과 반대.
❌ ④ capital became less important than labor in the new economy: 자본의 중요도 감소는 본문에 언급 없음.
det.tip: harvest cycles(자연 리듬) → clock-oriented(기계 리듬) = 사회 재편의 핵심.

ch: the rhythm of machines replaced the rhythm of nature in organizing society
farmers became wealthier than factory workers after industrialization
machines eventually stopped running because workers refused shifts
capital became less important than labor in the new economy

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 공장은 낮에만 가동할 수 있었다 — 불일치.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 공장은 낮 시간대에만 가동할 수 있었다: 본문은 'produce around the clock(24시간)'. 불일치.
❌ ② 24시간 돌아가는 기계가 가장 많은 위젯을 생산한다: 본문 일치.
❌ ③ 많은 공장에서 근무일은 8시간 교대조로 나뉜다: 본문 일치.
❌ ④ 임금은 노력과 생산에 연결되었다: 본문 일치.
det.tip: around the clock = 24시간 내내. 낮에만이 아님.

ch: 공장은 낮 시간대에만 가동할 수 있었다.
24시간 돌아가는 기계가 가장 많은 위젯을 생산한다.
많은 공장에서 근무일은 8시간 교대조로 나뉘어 있다.

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 산업화 이전의 노동은 수확 주기에 의해 이끌렸다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 기계 가동 시간이 길어져도 생산량은 같다: 본문은 시간이 길수록 더 많이 생산.
❌ ② 산업화는 근무 시간의 잠재 가치를 낮추었다: 본문은 raised(끌어올렸다).
✅ ③ 산업화 이전의 노동은 수확 주기에 의해 이끌렸다: 'previously guided by harvest cycles' — 일치.
❌ ④ 산업화 이후에도 사회는 재편되지 않았다: 'started to reorganize'로 재편됨.

ch: 기계 가동 시간이 길어져도 생산량은 동일하다.

questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 산업화가 가져온 시간과 노동의 관계 재편.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 산업화가 가져온 시간과 노동의 관계 재편: 시간·노동·자본의 관계 변화가 본문 전체.
❌ ① 현대 공장 기계의 에너지 효율: 에너지 효율 이야기 아님.
❌ ② 농경 사회의 수확 기법과 전통: 수확 주기는 배경으로만 등장.

det.analysis:

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 "the more hours you worked, the more widgets you produced, and the more money you made"가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 노동 시간·생산량·수입이 정비례 관계에 놓이게 되었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ Working hours, output, and income became directly proportional to one another.: 'the more ~ the more ~' 3단 반복이 시간·생산·수입의 정비례 관계를 나타냄.
❌ ① Workers could freely choose how many hours to work each day.: 자유 선택이 아닌 구조적 연결.
❌ ② Money was no longer necessary for purchasing factory goods.: 화폐 불필요는 본문 무관.
❌ ③ Machines worked harder than humans in every situation.: 기계 vs 인간 비교가 아님.
det.tip: the more A, the more B = A와 B의 정비례. 3단 반복은 시간·생산·수입 정비례.

ch: Workers could freely choose how many hours to work each day.

questions.passage: The arrival of the Industrial Age changed the relationship among time, labor, and capital. Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with greater speed and volume than ever before. A machine that runs twelve hours a day will produce more widgets than one that runs for only eight hours per day ― and a machine that runs twenty-four hours per day will produce the most widgets of all. As such, at many factories, the workday is divided into eight-hour shifts, so that there will always be people on hand to keep the widget machines humming. Industrialization raised the potential value of every single work hour ― the more hours you worked, the more widgets you produced, and the more money you made ― and thus wages became tied to effort and production. Labor, previously guided by harvest cycles, became clock-oriented, and society started to reorganize around new principles of productivity.
